statewide.text: On Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time, and anyone in line at 7 p.m. still gets to vote.
Every Florida county offers early voting from October 24 to October 31, and some counties offer extra days.
During early voting you can use any early voting site in the county where you are registered.
On Election Day you must vote at the polling place assigned to your precinct, which is listed on your voter information card and your county elections website.

Bring a current, valid ID that shows your photo and signature, such as a Florida driver license, Florida ID card, U.S. passport, debit or credit card, military ID, student ID, or veteran health ID card.
If your photo ID does not show your signature, bring a second ID that does.
If you do not have an accepted ID with you, you can still vote, but on a provisional ballot.
A picture of your ID on your phone does not count, so bring the actual card.
statewide.publisher: Hillsborough County Supervisor of Elections (2026 Voter Guide)

statewide.text: If you believe you are registered but your name cannot be found at your polling place, ask for a provisional ballot.
After voting a provisional ballot, you have until 5 p.m. on the second day after the election (Thursday, November 5) to give your Supervisor of Elections written proof that you are eligible.
A provisional ballot counts if you are eligible, you voted in the right precinct, and your signature matches the one on your voter record.
A mail ballot counts only if it reaches your county Supervisor of Elections by 7 p.m. on Election Day, and a postmark does not count.
The deadline to have a mail ballot sent to you was Thursday, October 22, 2026, so it is now too late to request one by mail.

You can still pick up your own mail ballot at your Supervisor of Elections office, but now that early voting has started you must sign a form saying an emergency keeps you from voting early or at your polling place.
If you asked for a mail ballot but would rather vote in person, bring the mail ballot with you, filled in or not.
You may bring a sample ballot or your own notes into the voting booth to help you remember your choices.

pinellas.mailBallotDropOff: Return your mail ballot to a Supervisor of Elections office or one of the secure ballot return locations listed at VotePinellas.gov so it arrives by 7 p.m. on November 3.

hillsborough.mailBallotDropOff: Drop your mail ballot in the secure ballot intake station inside any early voting site during early voting hours, or at a Supervisor of Elections office when it is open, so it arrives by 7 p.m. on November 3; polling places cannot accept it.
